Observation of Υ(1S) + Z associated production and measurement of the effective double-parton scattering cross section in proton-proton collisions at √ s = 13 TeV. 2 2026. A General Philosophy and Core Assumptions of the Methods One criticism or doubt that creeps into people’s minds about this idea is an uneasy feeling of model dependence or hidden assumptions; How sure are we about the correlation with impact parameter?; Is this relying too much on assuming the pythia model?, Is this simplified picture of independent multiparton interactions and impact parameter dependence correct? and other similar questions. There seems to be a worry that such questions may undermine the utility of such studies, but that’s not the case. Throughout this paper, I’ve used a definite model, in the form provided by Pythia which gives a useful example with concrete comparisons. Including model-specific information will also ultimately provide the most precise results wherever the model assumptions can be trusted or validated. However, the overall methodology and ideas behind the analysis follow from quite general approximations which have empirically been relatively succesful up to this point. The primary approximation upon which the methodology is built is: • The event can be factorized into activity from the hard scatter, and the rest of the event. Which is essentially the assumption that the factorization theorem holds for the hard process and that we have some experimental ability to isolate this process. From only this approximation we can see the utility of the cross-section ratio method, Ω.
